claim: The joint storage and reciprocal retrieval of learnt associated signals are presumably encoded by associative memory cells.
source: The joint storage and reciprocal retrieval of learnt associated signals are presumably encoded by associative memory cells.
evidence: This is a foundational assumption stated in the abstract that frames the research hypothesis.

claim: In the accumulation and enrichment of memory contents in lifespan, a signal often becomes a core signal associatively shared for other signals.
source: In the accumulation and enrichment of memory contents in lifespan, a signal often becomes a core signal associatively shared for other signals.
evidence: This is a general statement about memory organization based on the authors' conceptual framework.

claim: Mice experienced associative learning show whisker fluctuation induced by olfactory, gustatory, and tail-heating signals.
source: Mice experienced this associative learning show the whisker fluctuation induced by olfactory, gustatory, and tail-heating signals, or the other way around, that is, memories to multi-modal associated signals featured by their reciprocal retrievals.
evidence: This claim is supported by behavioral data presented in Figure 1 showing whisker motion responses to various stimuli.

claim: Barrel cortical neurons in mice that experienced associative learning become able to encode olfactory, gustatory, and tail-heating signals alongside the whisker signal.
source: Barrel cortical neurons in these mice become able to encode olfactory, gustatory, and tail-heating signals alongside the whisker signal.
evidence: This is supported by electrophysiological recordings shown in Figure 4 demonstrating neuronal responses to multiple stimuli.

claim: Barrel cortical neurons interconnect piriform, S1-Tr, and gustatory cortical neurons.
source: Barrel cortical neurons interconnect piriform, S1-Tr, and gustatory cortical neurons.
evidence: This is supported by neural tracing data in Figures 2 and 3 showing anatomical connections.

claim: With the barrel cortex as the hub, indirect activation occurs among piriform, gustatory, and S1-Tr cortices for the second-order associative memory.
source: With the barrel cortex as the hub, the indirect activation occurs among piriform, gustatory, and S1-Tr cortices for the second-order associative memory.
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data in Figure 5 showing cross-modal responses that bypass the whisker signal.

claim: Associative memory neurons recruited to encode multi-modal signals in the barrel cortex are downregulated by neuroligin-3 knockdown.
source: These associative memory neurons recruited to encode multi-modal signals in the barrel cortex for associative memory are downregulated by neuroligin-3 knockdown.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data in Figures 6-8 showing reduced memory formation and neuronal recruitment after neuroligin-3 knockdown.

claim: Associative memory neurons can be recruited as the core cellular substrate to memorize multiple associated signals by neuroligin-3-mediated synapse formation.
source: Thus, associative memory neurons can be recruited as the core cellular substrate to memorize multiple associated signals for the first-order and the second-order of associative memories by neuroligin-3-mediated synapse formation, which constitutes neuronal substrates of cognitive activities in the field of memoriology.
evidence: This conclusion integrates findings from behavioral, anatomical, and molecular experiments throughout the study.

claim: Associative learning and memory are major forms of information acquisition and storage.
source: Associative learning and memory are major forms of the information acquisition and storage (Byrne, 1987; Wasserman and Miller, 1997), in which multiple cross-modal signals are learnt associatively and memorized jointly (Feng et al., 2017; Vincis and Fontanini, 2016; Wang et al., 2015; Wang et al., 2013; Wang et al., 2019b).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to established literature in the field.

claim: Multiple cross-modal signals are learnt associatively and memorized jointly.
source: Associative learning and memory are major forms of the information acquisition and storage (Byrne, 1987; Wasserman and Miller, 1997), in which multiple cross-modal signals are learnt associatively and memorized jointly (Feng et al., 2017; Vincis and Fontanini, 2016; Wang et al., 2015; Wang et al., 2013; Wang et al., 2019b).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous research.

claim: Memories to associated signals are essential for cognitive activities and emotional responses.
source: Memories to associated signals have been thought to be essential for the cognitive activities and emotional responses (Wang et al., 2019b; Kandel and Pittenger, 1999; Poo et al., 2016; Silva et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: The cellular mechanism underlying associative memory was presumably based on activity-dependent strengthening in the interconnection of cell assemblies.
source: The cellular mechanism underlying associative memory was presumably based on an activity-dependent strengthening in the interconnection of cell assemblies (Hebb, 1949), which has been supported by synaptic and neuronal plasticity during the learning and memory (Armano et al., 2000; Bliss and Lømo, 1973; Bliss and Lynch, 1988; Lisman et al., 2018; Wang et al., 1997; Zhang et al., 2004).
evidence: This is based on Hebb's theory and supported by multiple citations to plasticity research.

claim: Activity-dependent plasticity in a single neural pathway cannot interpret associative memory featured by joint storage and reciprocal retrieval of associated signals from multiple pathways.
source: Although the neuronal plasticity influences the strengths in the formation of associative memory and the retrieval of memorized signals, this activity-dependent plasticity in a single neural pathway cannot interpret the associative memory featured by the joint storage and the reciprocal retrieval of associated signals specifically inputted from multiple pathways (Wang et al., 2019b).
evidence: This is a logical argument supported by citation that motivates the current research.

claim: Recent studies have discovered the recruitment of associative memory neurons in mice while they memorize associatively learnt signals.
source: Recent studies have discovered the recruitment of associative memory neurons in mice while they memorize the associatively learnt signals.
evidence: This is a summary statement introducing prior research findings.

evidence: This is supported by citations to previous molecular studies.

claim: Neuroligin-3 is one of the linkage proteins for synapse fixations.
source: Neuroligin-3 as one of the linkage proteins (Craig and Kang, 2007; Li et al., 2022; Lisé and El-Husseini, 2006; Südhof, 2017; Uchigashima et al., 2021) for synapse fixations has been examined, in which short-chain RNA (shRNA) specific for neurolingin-3 (Chang et al., 2006; Khatri et al., 2012; Pardridge, 2007; Pushparaj et al., 2008; Rao et al., 2009) was microinjected into the barrel cortex.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: The amplitudes of odorant-induced whisker motion are 20.11±0.8 degrees in neuroligin-3 knockdown mice and 32.11±0.65 degrees in shRNA scramble control mice.
source: After the paradigm of associative learning was processed to neuroligin-3 knockdown mice and shRNA scramble control mice, the amplitudes of odorant-induced whisker motion are 20.11±0.8 in neuroligin-3 knockdown mice (blue bar in Figure 6C, n=10) and 32.11±0.65 in shRNA scramble control mice (red bar, n=10; p<0.0001, one-way ANOVA).
evidence: This is quantitative behavioral data with statistical analysis from Figure 6C.

claim: The amplitudes of tailing-induced whisker motion are 18.62±1.26 degrees in neuroligin-3 knockdown mice and 32.54±1.12 degrees in shRNA scramble control mice.
source: The amplitudes of tailing-induced whisker motion are 18.62±1.26 in neuroligin-3 knockdown mice (blue bar in Figure 6C, n=10) and 32.54±1.12 in shRNA scramble control mice (red bar, n=10; p<0.0001, one-way ANOVA).
evidence: This is quantitative behavioral data with statistical analysis from Figure 6C.

claim: The amplitudes of sucrose-induced whisker motion are 20.22±0.9 degrees in neuroligin-3 knockdown mice and 32.54±1.12 degrees in shRNA scramble control mice.
source: The amplitudes of sucrose-induced whisker motion are 20.22±0.9 in neuroligin-3 knockdown mice (blue bar in Figure 6C, n=10) and 32.54±1.12 in shRNA scramble control mice (red bar, n=15; p<0.0001, one-way ANOVA).
evidence: This is quantitative behavioral data with statistical analysis from Figure 6C.

claim: The rates of avoidance to butyl acetate in whisking-induced olfactory responses are 55.63±3.55% in neuroligin-3 knockdown mice and 68.93±5.07% in shRNA scramble control mice.
source: On the other hand, the rates of avoidance to butyl acetate in whisking-induced olfactory responses are 55.63 ± 3.55% in neuroligin-3 knockdown mice (blue bar in the left panel of Figure 6D; n=15) and 68.93 ± 5.07% in shRNA scramble control mice (red bar; n=15, p<0.05, one-way ANOVA).
evidence: This is quantitative behavioral data with statistical analysis from Figure 6D.

claim: The durations of whisking-induced tail swing are 1.56±0.34 seconds in neuroligin-3 knockdown mice and 4.60±0.37 seconds in shRNA scramble mice.
source: The durations of whisking-induced tail swing are 1.56±0.34 s in neuroligin-3 knockdown mice (blue bar in Figure 6D, middle panel; n=10) and 4.60±0.37 s in shRNA scramble mice (red bar; n=10, p<0.0001, one-way ANOVA).
evidence: This is quantitative behavioral data with statistical analysis from Figure 6D.

claim: The times of whisking-induced lip lickings are 1.00±0.26 in neuroligin-3 knockdown mice and 4.20±0.36 in shRNA scramble control mice.
source: The times of whisking-induced lip lickings are 1.00±0.26 in neuroligin-3 knockdown mice (blue bar in right panel of Figure 6D; n=10) and 4.20±0.36 in shRNA scramble control mice (red bar; n=10, p<0.0001, one-way ANOVA).
evidence: This is quantitative behavioral data with statistical analysis from Figure 6D.

claim: Neuroligin-3 knockdown downregulates the joint storage and the reciprocal retrieval of the associated signals.
source: These results indicate that neuroligin-3 knockdown downregulates the joint storage and the reciprocal retrieval of the associated signals, in which the whisker signal is a core signal and the barrel cortex is a core place for these processes since neuroligin-3 knockdown has been executed in the barrel cortex.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the behavioral data from Figure 6C-D.

claim: The downregulation of reciprocal retrievals among olfactory, tailing, and gustatory signals by neuroligin-3 knockdown in the barrel cortex indicates that the indirect interaction among piriform, S1-Tr, and gustatory cortices is linked through the barrel cortex.
source: Therefore, the downregulation of the reciprocal retrievals among the olfactory signal, the tailing signal, and the gustatory signal by neuroligin-3 knockdown in the barrel cortex indicates that the indirect interaction among piriform, S1-Tr, and gustatory cortices is linked through the barrel cortex.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the behavioral data from Figure 6E-G showing effects of neuroligin-3 knockdown.

claim: The barrel cortex as a core station mediates the joint storage and the reciprocal retrieval of associated signals directly and indirectly.
source: Taking data in Figure 6 together, we suggest that the barrel cortex as a core station mediates the joint storage and the reciprocal retrieval of associated signals directly including the whisker signal with olfactory, gustatory, and somatic signals as well as indirectly among olfactory, somatic, and gustatory signals.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion integrating the behavioral data from Figure 6.

claim: The densities of synapse contacts from the S1-Tr cortex are 2.25±0.33 per 100 μm dendrite in scramble control subgroup and 0.35±0.13 in neuroligin-3 knockdown subgroup.
source: The densities of synapse contacts (contacts per 100 μm dendrite) from the S1-Tr cortex are 2.25±0.33 in scramble control subgroup (red bar in left columns of Figure 7C, n=20 dendrites from 5 mice) and 0.35±0.13 in neuroligin-3 knockdown subgroup (blue bar, n=20 dendrites from 5 mice; p<0.01, one-way ANOVA).
evidence: This is quantitative morphological data with statistical analysis from Figure 7C.

claim: Synapse contacts per 100 μm dendrite from the piriform cortex are 2.50±0.19 in scramble control subgroup and 0.30±0.15 in neuroligin-3 knockdown subgroup.
source: Synapse contacts per 100 μm dendrite from the piriform cortex are 2.50±0.19 in scramble control subgroup (red bar in right columns of Figure 7C, n=20 dendrites from 5 mice) and 0.30±0.15 in neuroligin-3 knockdown subgroup (blue bar, n=20 dendrites from 5 mice; p<0.01, one-way ANOVA).
evidence: This is quantitative morphological data with statistical analysis from Figure 7C.

claim: The learning-induced connection from the hippocampus to the barrel cortex disappears by the knockdown of barrel cortical neuroligin-3.
source: It is noteworthy that the learning-induced connection from the hippocampus to the barrel cortex disappears by the knockdown of barrel cortical neuroligin-3, indicating that new synapse innervations from the hippocampus to other cortices of memorizing specific signals is essential for the hippocampus to strengthen specific memory in cerebral cortices.
evidence: This is an observation from the neural tracing experiments with neuroligin-3 knockdown.

claim: New synapse innervations from the hippocampus to other cortices of memorizing specific signals is essential for the hippocampus to strengthen specific memory in cerebral cortices.
source: It is noteworthy that the learning-induced connection from the hippocampus to the barrel cortex disappears by the knockdown of barrel cortical neuroligin-3, indicating that new synapse innervations from the hippocampus to other cortices of memorizing specific signals is essential for the hippocampus to strengthen specific memory in cerebral cortices.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the anatomical data suggesting a functional role of hippocampal connections.

claim: Percentages of barrel cortical neurons in response to the whisker signal plus butyl acetate, tail-heating, and/or sucrose signal are 68% in the scramble control subgroup and 16.7% in neuroligin-3 knockdown subgroup.
source: Percentages of barrel cortical neurons in response to the whisker signal plus butyl acetate, tail-heating, and/or sucrose signal are 68% in the scramble control subgroup (n=50 neurons from 5 mice) and 16.7% in in neuroligin-3 knockdown subgroup (n=24 neurons from 5 mice, p<0.01, χ2-test in Figure 8C).
evidence: This is quantitative electrophysiological data with statistical analysis from Figure 8C.

claim: The learning-induced recruitment of associative memory neurons that encode multi-modal signals in the barrel cortex requires the synapse linkage mediated by neuroligin-3.
source: Thus, the learning-induced recruitment of associative memory neurons that encode multi-modal signals including the whisker, olfactory, tail, and gustatory signals in the barrel cortex requires the synapse linkage mediated by neuroligin-3.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the electrophysiological and morphological data from Figures 7-8.

claim: The reciprocal forms of associative memory are likely based on a process that the barrel cortex interconnects the piriform cortex, the S1-Tr cortex, and the gustatory cortex after learning.
source: These reciprocal forms of associative memory are likely based on a process that the barrel cortex interconnects the piriform cortex, the S1-Tr cortex, and the gustatory cortex, after the learning of such associated signals has been done and the memories to these associated signals are formed, as implied in previous studies (Feng et al., 2000; Wang et al., 2015; Gao et al., 2019; Liu et al., 2017; Yan et al., 2016).
evidence: This is an interpretation supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The coactivity of associative memory neurons may trigger the activation of intracellular Ca2+/calmodulin signaling pathway.
source: In addition, the coactivity of associative memory neurons may trigger the activation of intracellular Ca2+/calmodulin signaling pathway.
evidence: This is a mechanistic speculation about intracellular signaling.

claim: The Ca2+/calmodulin signaling pathway can initiate the conversion of silent synapses into functional synapses and inactive synapses into active synapses.
source: This signaling pathway can initiate the conversion of silent synapses into functional synapses and the conversion of inactive synapses into active synapses to strengthen the synapse-driving force and increase the activities of associative memory cells (Wang, 2019a; Liao et al., 1995; Wang and Kelly, 2001) as well as to upregulate neuron-encoding ability (Zhang et al., 2004; Chen et al., 2008), which leads to the strengthening of associative memory.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous mechanistic studies.

claim: The coactivity of the cerebral cortices in the associative learning induces the formation of their interconnection.
source: Thus, the coactivity of the cerebral cortices in the associative learning induces the formation of their interconnection, which can endorse the first order and the secondary order of associative memory.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion integrating the findings from the study.

claim: Associative memory neurons in the cerebral cortices are recruited by mutual synapse innervations based on neuroligin-3-mediated synapse linkage.
source: Associative memory neurons in the cerebral cortices are recruited by mutual synapse innervations based on neuroligin-3-mediated synapse linkage.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion integrating the molecular and anatomical findings.

claim: The learning of associated signals can be thought of as the coactivation of sensory cortices that encode these signals.
source: In this regard, the learning of associated signals can be thought of as the coactivation of sensory cortices that encode these signals.
evidence: This is a conceptual interpretation of the learning process.

claim: Associative memory can be thought of as the activity-dependent formation of new interconnections among cortices and convergent synapse innervations on coactive neurons.
source: Associative memory can be thought of as the activity-dependent formation of new interconnections among these cortices and the convergent synapse innervations on coactive neurons by new synapses and previous synapses, which is the feature of the recruitment of associative memory neurons in the early development to memorize unitary and simple signals, as well as the activity-dependent strengthening of these synapse connections among associative memory neurons in the following periods to memorize those complex signals organized from unitary/simple signals.
evidence: This is a conceptual framework integrating the findings of the study.

claim: The retrieval of associative memory can be thought of as the reactivation of associative memory neurons by exogenous cues or endogenous thinking.
source: The retrieval of associative memory can be thought of as the reactivation of these associative memory neurons by exogenous cues or endogenous thinking (Wang et al., 2019b).
evidence: This is a conceptual interpretation supported by citation.

claim: C57BL/6JThy1-YFP mice have glutamatergic neurons in the cerebral brain genetically labeled by YFP.
source: C57BL/6JThy1-YFP mice (Jackson Lab. JAX stock #003782, USA) were applied in our studies, whose glutamatergic neurons in the cerebral brain were genetically labeled by YFP (Feng et al., 2000; Zhang et al., 2013).
evidence: This describes the mouse model used in the study, supported by citations.

claim: AAV2/8-CMV-tdTomato is uptaken and expressed in the somata of barrel cortical neurons, and tdTomato is transported to their axonal boutons and terminals in the anterograde manner.
source: Theoretically and practically, AAV2/8-CMV-tdTomato was uptaken and then expressed in barrel cortical neurons, where the red fluorescent protein (RFP) was produced. The RFP, or tdTomato, was transported toward entire axons of such barrel cortical neurons at their target areas in an anterograde manner, such that axonal boutons and terminals were labeled by the RFP (Feng et al., 2017; Gao et al., 2016; Gao et al., 2019; Lei et al., 2017; Wu et al., 2020).
evidence: This describes the viral tracing methodology, supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: AAV/retro-CMV-EGFP is uptaken by axonal terminals and boutons, and then transported to the somata of cortical neurons in the retrograde manner.
source: AAV/retro-CMV-EGFP was uptaken by axonal terminals and boutons, and then was transported to the somata of cortical neurons in the retrograde manner for its expression and production, so that the sources of neuronal somata whose axons projected to the barrel cortex were tracked (Tervo et al., 2016).
evidence: This describes the retrograde viral tracing methodology, supported by citation.
